title: An Open-label Phase I/II Safety and Feasibility Basket Study of UKT-CART19.1
off: An Open-label Phase I/II, Single-center, Interventional Singlearm Basket Trial of UKT-CART19.1 in Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Autoimmune Diseases

officials.a: University Hospital , Department of Internal Medicine II

summary: An open-label phase I/II, single-center, interventional single-arm basket trial of UKT-CART19.1 in patients with relapsed/refractory autoimmune diseases
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Patients at least 18 years of age, and ≤ 80 years old at the time of signing the informed consent
2. Signed and dated informed consent by participants before conduct of any trial-specific procedure
3. One of the following diseases according to the EULAR/ACR criteria (see appendices) for IIM/AAV/RA/SSc; McDonald criteria Wingerchuk et al., 2015; KKNMS; Sechi et al., 2022 for MS or clinical standards for PV and ITP plus disease active according to the specific disease as follows:

   * Idiopathic inflammatory myositis (IIM): Disease activity defined by CK \> 3x ULN and clinical symptoms and / or disease activity documented by MRI
   * ANCA associated vasculitis (AAV): Disease activity defined as BVAS-3 new/worse \> 6, i.e. ongoing or new organ damage (lung, kidney or CNS)
   * Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA): Disease activity defined DAS28 \> 4
   * Pemphigus vulgaris (PV): Disease activity defined by PDAI \>15 points
   * Multiple sclerosis (MS): clinical activity previous 24 months: greater than or equal to 1 relapse with or without increase of EDSS, clinical progression previous 24 months: increase of EDSS 1 or increase in other MS-related measures (such as 25FWT, 9HPT, SDMT), MRI activity previous 24 months: greater than or equal to 1 Gd+ lesion or new or new enlarging T2-hyperintense lesion greater than or equal to 3 mm, failure of greater than or equal to 2 high efficacy therapy (not included in AHCST criteria)
   * Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP): Disease activity defined as thrombocytes \<30.000/µl and/or \<50.000/µl and signs of bleeding
   * Systemic scleriosis (SSc): Disease activity defined as a worsening of mRSS \> 25% and/or decline of FVC \>10% and/or decline of DLCO \>15% (of predicted values) and/or new organ involvement (heart, kidney)

   AND refractory to at least (but not limited) to 2 immunosuppressive disease-specific standard treatment:
   * IIM: greater than or equal to 2 standard treatments in accordance with the current AWMF S2k Guideline (S2kLeitlinie Myositissyndrome. Version: 6.0 Stand: 28.04.2022 Gültig bis: 27.04.2027)
   * AAV: greater than or equal to 2 standard treatments in accordance with EULAR recommendations (Hellmich B et al. EULAR recommendations for the management of ANCA-associated vasculitis: 2022 update. Ann Rheum Dis. 2024 Jan 2;83(1):30-47. doi: 10.1136/ard-2022-223764. PMID: 36927642.
   * RA: greater than or equal to 4 standard treatments in accordance with the current EULAR Recommendations for the Management of RA (Smolen J et al. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases, 2026; 85, 991-1009)
   * PV: greater than or equal to 2 standard treatments in accordance with the current S2k Guideline (S2k-Leitlinie Diagnostik und Therapie des Pemphigus vulgaris / foliaceus und des bullösen Pemphigoids. Version: 3.0 Stand: 01.04.2026 Gültig bis: 31.03.2031).
   * MS: greater than or equal to 2 high efficacy therapy ("Wirksamkeitskategorie 3") in accordance with the current S2k Guideline (Hemmer B. et al., Diagnose und Therapie der Multiplen Sklerose, Neuromyelitis-optica-Spektrum-Erkrankung (NMOSD) und MOG-IgG-assoziierten Erkrankung (MOGAD), S2k-Leitlinie, 2026, in: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Neurologie (Hrsg.), Leitlinien für Diagnostik und Therapie in der Neurologie. Online: www.dgn.org/leitlinien (abgerufen am 15.06.2026)
   * ITP: failure of at least Glucocorticoids, Thrombopoetin receptor agonists (TPO-RA) and Fostamatinib in accordance with the current Onkopedia Guideline (DGHO Deutsche Gesellschaft für Hämatologie und Medizinische Onkologie e. V. (Hrsg.): Immunthrombozytopenie (ITP). Onkopedia Leitlinie. Stand: August 2024. https://www.onkopedia.com/de/onkopedia/guidelines/immunthrombozytopenie-itp (Abgerufen am: 15.06.2026))
   * SSc: greater than or equal to 2 standard of care systemic treatment in accordance with the current EULAR Recommendations ( Del Galdo F et alEULAR recommendations for the treatment of systemic sclerosis: 2023 update Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases Published Online First: 11 October 2024. doi: 10.1136/ard-2024-226430)
4. Male participants able to father children and female participants of childbearing potential must practice true abstinence or agree to use 2 highly effective methods (i.e. those that result in a low failure rate (i.e., \< 1% per year) of contraception throughout the duration of the study. Male fertile subjects must also not donate sperm during the study and for at least 12 months following the UKT-CART19.1 infusion
5. Female Subject of childbearing potential and male subjects with female partner of childbearing potential is willing to use highly effective contraceptive methods during treatment until 12 months after IMP exposure.

   For the purpose of this document, a woman is considered of childbearing potential (WOCBP), i.e. fertile, following menarche and until becoming post-menopausal unless permanently sterile. Permanent sterilisation methods include hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy and bilateral oophorectomy. A postmenopausal state is defined as no menses for 12 months without an alternative medical cause. A high follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) level in the postmenopausal range may be used to confirm apostmenopausal state in women not using hormonal contraception or hormonal replacement therapy. However, in the absence of 12 months of amenorrhea, a single FSH measurement is insufficient. For the purpose of this document, a man is considered fertile after puberty unless permanently sterile by bilateral orchidectomy. Highly effective methods are defined as those that result in a low failure rate (ie, less than 1% per year) when used consistently and correctly. The following are highly effective methods of contraception:
   * combined (estrogen and progestogen containing) hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation 1: - oral - intravaginal - transdermal
   * progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation1:
   * oral
   * injectable
   * implantable2
   * intrauterine device (IUD) 2
   * intrauterine hormone-releasing system (IUS)2
   * bilateral tubal occlusion2
   * vasectomised partner2,3
   * sexual abstinence4

     1. Hormonal contraception may be susceptible to interaction with the IMP, which may reduce the efficacy of the contraception method.
     2. Contraception methods that in the context of this guidance are considered to have low user dependency.
     3. Vasectomised partner is a highly effective birth control method provided that partner is the sole sexual partner of the WOCBP trial participant and that the vasectomised partner has received medical assessment of the surgical success.
     4. In the context of this guidance sexual abstinence is considered a highly effective method only if defined as refraining from heterosexual intercourse during the entire period of risk associated with the study treatments. The reliability of sexual abstinence needs to be evaluated in relation to the duration of the clinical trial and the preferred and usual lifestyle of the subject. Woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must also: - Have a negative pregnancy test as verified by the Investigator, one negative serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) pregnancy test result at screening, prior to LD. This applies even if the subject practices true abstinence from heterosexual contact. - Perform pregnancy testing every month for 6 months after IMP administration. A home test is sufficient.
   * Agree to abstain from breastfeeding during study participation and for at least 12 months after IMP administration.
6. All subjects must agree to refrain from donating blood while on study drug and for 1 year after discontinuation from this study treatment.
7. Absolute CD3+ T cell count ≥100/μl at time of leukapheresis
8. Subject must have Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 2
9. Subject must have recovery to Grade 1 or baseline of any non-hematologic toxicities due to prior treatments, excluding alopecia and Grade 2 neuropathy
10. Subject must have adequate vascular access for leukapheresis
11. Subject must understand and voluntarily sign an ICF prior to any study-related assessments/procedures being conducted
12. Subject is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements as well as agrees to continued follow up for up to 15 years as mandated by the regulatory guidelines for gene therapy trials

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Subject used any investigational agents within 15 days of leukapheresis
2. Contraindications to the IMP and its components, including but not limited to hypersensitivity to the CAR-T cell product, excipients, lymphodepleting agents and/or tocilizumab.
3. Subject received any of the following within the last 7 days of leukapheresis:

   Major surgery (as defined by the investigator) Radiation therapy Use of any systemic anti-neoplastic drug therapy
4. Patients who have previously received gene therapy
5. History or presence of clinically relevant CNS pathology other than the underlying diseases in this protocol, such as epilepsy, seizure, paresis, aphasia, stroke, subarachnoid hemorrhage or other CNS bleed, severe brain injuries, dementia, Parkinson's disease, cerebellar disease, organic brain syndrome, or psychosis.
6. Subject has any of the following laboratory abnormalities:

   Absolute lymphocyte count \<100/µL at time of leukapheresis Serum Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) \< 30 mL/min Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) \> 3 × upper limit of normal (ULN), non-Myositis related Serum total bilirubin \> 3.0 mg/dL for subjects with documented Gilbert's syndrome
7. Echocardiography (ECHO) or MRI with left ventricular ejection fraction \< 40%
8. Subject with a history of Class III or IV congestive heart failure (CHF)
9. Subject with a history of myocardial infarction within the last 12 months
10. Patients unable to stop immunosuppressive treatment prior to leukapheresis (AZA, TAC, MMF, CYC, mitoxantrone, JAK inhibitors, or GC at prednisolone equivalent dose \>10mg/day). Intermittent topical, inhaled or intranasal corticosteroids are allowed
11. Subject is positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1), uncontrolled hepatitis B or C
12. Subject with FVC \<45%, and/or DLCO (corrected for Hb) \<30%
13. Subjects with pulmonary comorbidities (including but not limited to active smoking habits, oxygen requirements, and severe asthma)
14. Subject has uncontrolled systemic fungal, bacterial, viral or other infection (including tuberculosis) despite appropriate antibiotics or other treatment
15. Subject with prior history of malignancies, unless the subject has been free of the disease for ≥ 1year with the exception of the following non-invasive malignancies:

    * Basal cell carcinoma of the skin
    * Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
    * Carcinoma in situ of the cervix
    * Carcinoma in situ of the breast
    * Incidental histologic finding of prostate cancer (T1a or T1b using the TNM \[tumor, nodes, metastasis\] clinical staging system) or prostate cancer that is curative
16. Subject is a female who is pregnant, nursing, or breastfeeding, or who intends to become pregnant during participation in the study
17. Subject has any significant medical condition, laboratory abnormality, or psychiatric illness that would prevent the subject from participating in the study
18. Subject has any condition including the presence of laboratory abnormalities, which places the subject at unacceptable risk if he/she were to participate in the study

arms.d: Open-label, single centre, non-randomized, non-comparative, Phase I/II basket study of safety and feasibility

primary.m: Safety of UKT-CART19.1 in refractory and/or relapsed autoimmune diseases

x.titre: CAR-T anti-CD19 (UKT-CART19.1) dans les maladies auto-immunes réfractaires : essai panier de phase 1/2
x.question: Les CAR-T anti-CD19 UKT-CART19.1 sont-ils faisables et sûrs dans plusieurs maladies auto-immunes en rechute ou réfractaires ?
x.contexte:
Une proportion de patients atteints de maladies auto-immunes sévères (vascularite à ANCA, myopathie inflammatoire, polyarthrite rhumatoïde, sclérodermie systémique, pemphigus, PTI, sclérose en plaques) reste en échec des immunosuppresseurs et biothérapies usuels. Dans ces maladies, les lymphocytes B autoréactifs et les plasmablastes jouent un rôle central.

Les lymphocytes T à récepteur chimérique d'antigène (CAR-T) dirigés contre CD19, développés d'abord en hématologie, éliminent en profondeur les lymphocytes B. Les premières séries, surtout dans le lupus, ont rapporté des rémissions prolongées sans traitement de fond, ce qui a conduit à les tester dans d'autres maladies. Cet essai monocentrique de l'hôpital universitaire de Tübingen est un essai panier à un seul bras, non comparatif : 36 patients sont traités par UKT-CART19.1, avec un critère d'activité et de réfractarité propre à chaque maladie (par exemple DAS28 > 4 dans la PR, BVAS > 6 dans les vascularites, aggravation du score cutané de Rodnan ou de la CVF dans la sclérodermie). L'objectif principal est la tolérance à 6 mois.
x.interet: L'étude apportera des données de tolérance sur un CAR-T académique dans plusieurs maladies auto-immunes. Elle ne permettra pas de conclure sur l'efficacité, vu l'absence de comparateur et les petits effectifs par maladie.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 80 ans atteints d'une maladie auto-immune active, réfractaire à au moins deux traitements standards.
inclusion: Une des maladies suivantes : myopathie inflammatoire, vascularite à ANCA, PR, sclérodermie, pemphigus vulgaire, PTI ou sclérose en plaques
Maladie active selon des seuils propres à chaque pathologie (CPK, BVAS, DAS28, PDAI, EDSS/IRM, plaquettes, mRSS/CVF/DLCO)
Réfractaire à au moins 2 traitements standards (4 dans la PR)
exclusion: Non précisé dans l'extrait disponible du registre

bras.traitement: Lymphocytes T CAR anti-CD19 autologues (UKT-CART19.1), ouvert, non randomisé

x.duree: Suivi principal de 6 mois (étude jusqu'à environ 2028)
x.critere: Tolérance de UKT-CART19.1 dans les maladies auto-immunes réfractaires, à 6 mois.
